title: Characters of a smooth connected group have no torsion
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups below are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $X^*(G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{F\text{-grp}}(G,\mathbf G_m)$ for the abelian group of characters, with addition given by multiplication of values, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. For every smooth connected group $G$, the abelian group $X^*(G)$ is torsion free: for every integer $n\geq1$ and every character $\chi$, the identity $\chi^n=1$ of group-scheme morphisms implies $\chi=1$.

source.place: Proposition 18.19, proof, printed p.392; Theorem 18.25, proof, printed p.393: X(G) is torsion-free because G is smooth and connected.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], the smooth $F$-scheme $G$ is regular and locally Noetherian. It is nonempty (its identity is an $F$-point) and connected, so [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] makes it integral. Applying [def-pc-integral-scheme] to the nonempty affine open $G$ itself shows that $A$ is an integral domain.

source.place: Tag 056S, lemma-smooth-regular; properties.tex Tags 0569, lemma-regular-normal, and 033N, lemma-normal-locally-Noetherian.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$ and $\chi^n=1$. By the affine contravariance of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}F[t,t^{-1}]$ of [def-sc-gm-ga], the character corresponds to an $F$-algebra map $\chi^*:F[t,t^{-1}]\to A$. Set $u=\chi^*(t)$. The multiplication formula $m^*(t)=t\otimes t$ makes the coordinate of $\chi^n$ equal to $u^n$, while the trivial character sends $t$ to $1$; hence $u^n=1$ in $A$.

source.place: Proposition 18.19, proof, printed p.392; Theorem 18.25, proof, printed p.393; explicit coordinate-ring argument supplying the implicit torsion-freeness assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] to the nonzero polynomial $T^n-1\in F[T]$. Its leading coefficient is $1$, so $T^n-1=\prod_j(T-a_j)$ with $a_j\in F$. Evaluate this finite product at $u$ in $A$ to obtain $0=\prod_j(u-a_j1_A)$. In a domain a finite product is zero only if one factor is zero, by induction using the absence of zero divisors (the empty product is $1\ne0$). Thus $u=a_j1_A$ for some $j$. Repeated roots cause no difficulty.

source.place: Proposition 18.19, proof, printed p.392; Theorem 18.25, proof, printed p.393; explicit coordinate-ring argument supplying the implicit torsion-freeness assertion.

proof.text: The identity section of [def-sc-group-scheme] gives an $F$-algebra map $\epsilon:A\to F$. A group homomorphism preserves the identity: its value there is an idempotent in the group $F^\times$, hence $1$. Therefore $\epsilon(u)=1$; since $u=a_j1_A$, this says $a_j=1$ and hence $u=1$. The map $\chi^*$ now fixes scalars and sends both $t$ and $t^{-1}$ to $1$, so on every Laurent monomial, and thus every finite Laurent sum, it agrees with the trivial character. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\chi=1$ as a scheme morphism and hence as a group-scheme morphism. This proves the asserted torsion-freeness.
